candidates.title: Peripheral real-time grocery-data infrastructure
candidates.shift: A hobbyist API/MCP exposing live New Zealand supermarket pricing suggests retail data may become an openly queryable utility layer, not just an internal analytics asset.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if real-time price/inventory feeds become expected public infrastructure, store operators everywhere may face pressure to expose data they currently guard — starting, oddly, in a small periphery market.
candidates.evidence: Show HN: 'Spread' — real-time NZ supermarket data via API and MCP, single low-traction post.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of retail data moving from proprietary system-of-record to open queryable infrastructure; if it spreads, store ops and pricing strategy become semi-public and machine-readable in real time.

candidates.title: Store as climate refuge
candidates.shift: Retail storefronts (ice cream shops) are being explicitly framed and designed as places of thermal respite during extreme heat, not just commerce.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative/Trend-adjacent: as heatwaves intensify, small-format retail may increasingly market itself on cooling/shelter value — a reframing of storefronts as public thermal infrastructure, not just POS.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen roundup of five ice cream shops framed explicitly as 'cool respite' amid heatwaves and UK's hottest summer on record.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from store-as-transaction-site to store-as-climate-shelter; driven by rising ambient heat. If it scales, retail HVAC/design specs and even zoning could start treating certain stores as quasi-public cooling infrastructure.
candidates.author: Cajsa Carlson

candidates.title: Interlocking-volume housing as land-efficiency construction method
candidates.shift: A Dutch 'Tetris'-style interlocking dual-family house shows a construction approach to maximizing density on constrained urban/riverside plots via geometric interlocking rather than stacking.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could inform mixed-use/retail-adjacent infill on tight urban parcels — an alternative to podium/tower typologies when land is scarce but zoning allows creative massing.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen coverage of Woonpioniers' CoHouse — two interlocking family homes in one gabled volume on a Utrecht riverside plot.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of construction geometry (interlocking massing) as a land-scarcity solution; if adapted to mixed-use, could reshape how retail-plus-residential infill gets built on small urban parcels.
candidates.author: Starr Charles

candidates.title: Community canteen as retail-edge social infrastructure
candidates.shift: A community canteen embedded into a fragmented retail/residential urban edge in China functions less as standalone food service and more as connective community infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: ground-floor retail edges may increasingly be programmed as community food/gathering infrastructure rather than pure commerce — blurring retail and civic space, first visible in Chinese new-town development.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily feature on Community Canteen No. 11 in Aranya Qinhuangdao, sited among apartments, ground-floor retail, and a park, designed as connective rather than standalone.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of retail-adjacent space being reprogrammed toward community/connection value over pure transaction; if it spreads, mall/strip developers may prioritize canteen-like anchor community spaces over anchor retail.
candidates.author: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang

candidates.title: Peri-urban Southeast Asia commercial districts forming around gathering spaces
candidates.shift: A cafe in a newly developed, still-sparse commercial district outside Makassar, Indonesia, is positioned as an early anchor for community gathering ahead of dense urban fabric forming.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: peripheral/emerging commercial districts in Southeast Asia may be forming around social/gathering anchors before retail density arrives — inverting the usual retail-first-then-community sequence.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily coverage of Common Days Cafe in Maros, near Makassar, Indonesia, in a sparse newly developed commercial district.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of periphery commercial development sequencing gathering-space-first, retail-later; if a pattern, it suggests site-selection models for emerging-market retail should track cafe/community anchors as leading indicators.
candidates.author: Pratik Mour

candidates.title: Industrial warehouse adaptive reuse into timber office
candidates.shift: A textile warehouse near Barcelona is being converted into an office using inserted timber partitions within the existing concrete-and-brick shell, rather than demolition.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: adaptive reuse using lightweight timber insertion (rather than full retrofit) could be a low-carbon, low-cost template for converting obsolete industrial/retail stock into office or mixed-use space.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen feature on NUA Arquitectures' renovation of the Tuvatèxtil warehouse near Barcelona using timber partitions within existing masonry structure.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of circular-economy construction: reusing industrial shells with lightweight timber inserts rather than demolishing. If scaled, could offer retailers a template for converting dead retail/industrial stock cheaply and with lower embodied carbon.
candidates.author: Jon Astbury

candidates.title: Absence of indoor micro-navigation standard for large facilities
candidates.shift: GNSS-based navigation fails inside large campuses, government complexes, and (by extension) big-box/mall facilities; researchers propose a Web-GIS + volunteered-geographic-info framework to fill the granular indoor routing gap.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: names a real absence — no standard for facility-level indoor wayfinding data — that becomes more urgent as physical AI (robots, delivery, autonomous carts) needs precise indoor maps of stores/warehouses.
candidates.evidence: Study proposing a Web-GIS framework combining volunteered geographic information and satellite imagery for smart campus/facility indoor navigation, citing the GNSS granularity gap.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of a missing standard: indoor/facility-scale spatial data infrastructure. As robotics and physical AI enter stores and warehouses, the absence of a granular indoor-mapping standard becomes an operational bottleneck worth watching.
candidates.author: Warekuromor Tubolayefa (PhD), Adepoju Olumide Mathew (PhD), Alaga Abayomi Taofeek (PhD) et al.

candidates.title: Building-level microgrid reconfiguration for energy optimization
candidates.shift: A data-driven framework proposes dynamically reconfiguring building-level energy microgrids using real-time sensing and load forecasting, treating the building itself as an adaptive energy node.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: touches the open 'compute?/utilities' hunt zone — buildings (including big-box stores) may need to manage energy as a dynamically reconfigurable microgrid rather than a static utility hookup, especially as compute/EV/refrigeration loads grow.
candidates.evidence: Study proposing hierarchical data-driven dynamic reconfiguration and energy-saving optimization for building energy-consuming microgrids using multi-source sensing and load forecasting.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of buildings shifting from passive energy consumers to actively managed microgrid nodes; if adopted at store scale, facilities teams would need new skills/contracts for real-time load balancing and topology optimization.
candidates.author: S.L. Liu, D. T. Liu

candidates.title: Far-UVC disinfection moving from health facilities into transit/public spaces
candidates.shift: 222nm far-UVC lamps, previously discussed mainly for hospitals, are being tested for continuous airborne/surface disinfection inside railway trains — a mass-transit, high-occupancy public space.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative cross-branch signal: if far-UVC proves viable in trains, similar continuous disinfection infrastructure could migrate into high-traffic retail spaces (transit-adjacent stores, food halls), becoming a new fixture spec and insurance/health-code consideration.
candidates.evidence: Study on effectiveness of 222nm far-UVC disinfection of airborne and surface bioaerosols specifically tested in railway train environments.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of health-infrastructure spec migrating from clinical settings into public/transit space; if it continues, far-UVC fixtures could become an expected build-out item for high-footfall retail and transit-adjacent stores.
candidates.author: X. Wang, Kangqi Guo, Wenjie Huang et al.

candidates.title: Remote-sensing-mapped urban heat risk from land-use change
candidates.shift: Multi-source satellite data is being used to map how specific land-cover transitions (not just urbanization broadly) drive land-surface heat exposure risk at fine spatial resolution.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: finer-grained heat-risk mapping tied to specific land-use transitions could feed into site-selection and real-estate underwriting models, letting retailers/insurers price heat exposure at the parcel level rather than city level.
candidates.evidence: Study using 2000/2010/2020 multi-source remote sensing in Zhejiang Province linking specific land-cover transitions to land-surface heat exposure risk.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of climate-risk data granularity increasing from city-level to parcel/land-cover-transition level; if adopted by insurers/site-selectors, real-estate heat-risk pricing could become far more precise and locally differentiated.
candidates.author: Yuansheng Huang, Zhang Weixiao, Mengmeng Shi et al.

candidates.title: Construction-waste framework emerging in Afghanistan's expanding building sector
candidates.shift: Afghanistan's rapidly expanding construction sector is prompting development of a dedicated sustainable construction-waste-reduction framework — a governance category that didn't previously exist there.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence-signal: a fragile/peripheral market building its own construction-waste standard from scratch, rather than importing one — worth watching as a case of periphery setting rather than receiving regulatory frameworks.
candidates.evidence: Study developing an integrated sustainable construction waste reduction and management framework for Afghanistan's construction sector, addressing barriers to implementation.
candidates.source: Scientific Journal of Engineering and Technology
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of a peripheral, low-regulation construction market originating its own waste-governance category rather than adopting a Western standard; if it matures, could offer a low-cost template for other fast-growing, low-oversight construction markets.
candidates.author: Qais Mohammad Samsor, Amanullah Faqiri, Mohammad Najim Wahedy et al.

candidates.title: Absence of a post-disaster building-stock circularity framework
candidates.shift: Post-disaster damaged building stock is reframed as an underused circular-economy resource, with researchers proposing a strategic-autonomy assessment framework rather than treating it as simple demolition waste.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence-signal: no standard category yet exists for valuing/quantifying disaster-damaged building stock as a circular resource — relevant to retailers with real estate in climate-disaster-exposed regions facing repeated rebuild cycles.
candidates.evidence: Study proposing a circular-economy assessment framework for post-disaster building stock through a strategic-management/resilience lens, noting circularity potential is currently unquantified.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of a missing financial/regulatory category: disaster-damaged real estate as a circular resource rather than sunk loss. If it matures, insurers, reconstruction contracts, and REIT accounting could gain a new 'circular resilience value' line item for climate-exposed stores.
candidates.author: Тетяна Шевченко, Julian Kirchherr, Meisam Ranjbari et al.

candidates.title: Cement/concrete industry pressured toward circular decarbonization by 2050
candidates.shift: EU cement and concrete industry is combining prospective life-cycle assessment with participatory foresight to identify circular-economy pathways for a mandated 2050 decarbonization target.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative/Trend-adjacent: already a known decarbonization push, but the pairing of LCA with participatory foresight signals concrete/cement specs for new construction (including retail buildouts) could shift materially within the next decade.
candidates.evidence: Study enriching prospective life-cycle assessment of EU cement/concrete circular economy strategies with participatory foresight, tied to 2050 decarbonization urgency.
candidates.source: The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment
candidates.initial_analysis: Already a known decarbonization trajectory; included for context/calibration. If circular cement pathways mature, retail construction specs and cost structures for new-build stores could shift materially by H3.
candidates.author: Anna M. Walker, Cristian Matti, Paola Federica Albizzati et al.

candidates.title: Embodied-carbon life-cycle thinking entering mainstream architectural practice
candidates.shift: A new book positions life-cycle assessment/embodied-carbon thinking as a standard part of the architectural design process, while noting cost and social dimensions remain underdeveloped.
candidates.ai_read: Trend: embodied-carbon awareness in design is already well underway and widely covered — included for context; the noted gap (cost/social LCA) is the more interesting unresolved thread for retail construction economics.
candidates.evidence: New book 'Life Cycle Thinking for Architectural Design' framing LCA/embodied carbon as increasingly commonplace in architectural discourse, while cost and social LCA remain underdeveloped.
candidates.initial_analysis: Already a mainstream design trend (embodied carbon/LCA); flagged mainly because the acknowledged absence of cost/social LCA integration is the sharper edge — a missing standard for pricing embodied-carbon tradeoffs in retail construction decisions.
candidates.author: Naomi Keena

candidates.title: AI-driven omnichannel retail decision orchestration (literature review)
candidates.shift: A systematic literature review argues AI is moving omnichannel retail from parallel customer-analytics/ops streams toward integrated real-time decision orchestration.
candidates.ai_read: Hype: this is a literature-review synthesis of an already widely covered trend (AI omnichannel orchestration) with no new instance or deployment — included for Kristen's calibration, likely Context rather than signal.
candidates.evidence: Journal article presenting a systematic literature review and integrated decision-intelligence framework for AI-driven omnichannel retail management.
candidates.source: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science
candidates.initial_analysis: A synthesis piece, not a new development — already-named trend of AI orchestrating omnichannel retail decisions. Included at low priority for Kristen's own filtering judgment rather than as a fresh signal.
candidates.author: Pratap Kumar Sahu

candidates.title: Climate-comfort landscape design applied to tourism/scenic commercial areas
candidates.shift: A study optimizes landscape morphology (shading, vegetation, terrain form) specifically for climatic comfort in a rural mountain-forest scenic/tourism area under heat stress.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: niche academic case study, but the underlying method (engineering outdoor landscape form for thermal comfort) could migrate to outdoor retail/lifestyle-center design as heat stress increases visitor discomfort at open-air commercial sites.
candidates.evidence: Case study of Western Sichuan Bamboo Sea Scenic Area optimizing landscape morphology for climatic comfort using field measurements of temperature/humidity under a climate-ecological compensation framework.
candidates.initial_analysis: A niche case study in landscape thermal-comfort engineering; if methods generalize, outdoor retail/lifestyle centers in hot climates may start specifying landscape morphology (not just shade structures) as a design requirement.
candidates.author: L. L. Fan, F. Zhang

candidates.title: Developer-branded office space as cultural signaling
candidates.shift: A real-estate developer in Panama commissions offices explicitly designed to embody its brand values (craftsmanship, tradition) in daily spatial experience for staff.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative/minor: single instance of a Latin American real-estate developer using its own headquarters as a branding exercise — could reflect a broader move toward developer HQs as showrooms for construction/material capability.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily feature on Sartoriale Offices in Panama City, designed as a spatial interpretation of the real-estate developer's brand values.
candidates.initial_analysis: Single instance of developer-as-brand-experience in Latin America; weak but flags a pattern where real-estate firms use owned HQ space to market capability/culture directly to tenants and partners.
candidates.author: Valentina Díaz
